A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CCDB research. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v3's five-page supplement. Material moved from v1's main text can be matched reliably to v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original CCDB classification results on five datasets, together with ablations, feature analyses, attention visualizations and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains the original CCDB benchmark results in Tables 1–2 and the experimental analyses across the main text and supplement.

M1.justification: The compactness regularizer changes from normalization by n_c in v1 Equation 8 to n_k(n_k-1) in v3 Equation 7, changing the stated loss's scaling. The three-stage pipeline, distribution matching, softmax weights, clipping and weighted sampling remain. The PDFs do not establish whether implementation or experimental runs changed.

E1.justification: Both evaluate cMNIST, cCIFAR10, Waterbirds, CelebA and CivilComments with the same classification tasks and spurious attributes. The toy scenarios also remain. Renaming the synthetic-data section to multi-class data does not introduce new coverage.

E2.justification: v1 Table III and v3 Table 1 contain the same GroupDRO, LFF, LC, ERM and uLA comparators. The real-world comparisons retain the same additional JTT, SELF, MASKTUNE and XRM entries, including identical dataset participation and missing-result cells.

E3.justification: Dataset splits and counts, bias-conflicting ratios, architectures, training budgets, augmentations, metrics and model-selection procedures remain unchanged. v1 Tables I–II match supplementary Tables 3–4 in v3; relocated training and model-selection descriptions preserve the reported settings.

E4.justification: The split-ratio and clipping sweeps, compactness ablations, model-selection curves, weight histograms, feature-correlation analyses, attention examples and computational analysis are retained. v3's supplementary experimental sections largely relocate v1's existing analyses; the combined main-text Figure 4 redisplays existing evidence.

E5.justification: Both report benchmark results over five random seeds and retain the same standard-deviation reporting and plotted uncertainty. No additional repeated-run information, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores, computational measurements and empirical figure contents are retained after matching relocated material. For example, CCDB worst-group accuracies remain 90.48±0.28 on Waterbirds, 85.27±0.28 on CelebA and 75.00±0.26 on CivilComments. No new empirical result entries or revised findings were identified.

T1.justification: v3 adds a formal causal account in Section 3 and supplementary Section 7: causal graphs, domain-invariance assumptions, backdoor adjustment and a one-to-one core-feature/label assumption connecting covariate balance to CCDB. It also removes v1's unsupported general equivalence between minimizing mutual information and maximizing conditional entropy, explicitly adopting negative conditional entropy as the objective.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions now describe maximizing conditional label entropy instead of simply minimizing mutual information. The introduction additionally claims consistency with causal covariate balancing. The central claims about annotation-free distribution balancing, class balancing and competitive performance remain.

C2.justification: v3 interprets distribution matching as removing confounding through covariate balance and explains which mechanisms vary across domains. This extends v1's distributional explanation under explicit causal assumptions. Existing experimental interpretations remain, while the blanket statement that the method 'has no limitations' is removed.

D1.justification: v3 Algorithm 1 omits v1's specification that sample-weight logits start at -1 and drops its random-network-initialization wording. Optimizer settings, pretraining, hyperparameters, hardware and computational measurements are otherwise retained, principally in the supplement.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Neal's causal-inference notes, Kullback and Leibler, and Yin et al.'s causal-estimation work, supporting the new covariate-balance positioning. Several background references are removed, while the principal relationships to stable learning and group-robust methods remain.

P1.justification: The journal-style manuscript is reorganized into a main paper and separately paginated supplement. Related work is condensed in the main text, while detailed discussion, settings and several analyses move to the supplement. Substantial prose editing accompanies terminology changes from 'causal' to 'core' and 'bias-free' to 'bias-agnostic'.

P2.justification: v3 adds causal diagrams to Figure 1 and supplementary Figure 6, combines sensitivity plots with selected correlation panels in Figure 4, and extensively relocates existing figures and tables. The document template, figure sizing, captions, table placement and overall layout are substantially revised.

improvement.justification: v3 improves conceptual clarity by removing the unsupported general mutual-information/conditional-entropy equivalence and explicitly explaining the spurious-feature approximation. The causal account makes its assumptions inspectable, and the reorganized presentation preserves the empirical evidence. However, the loss rescaling is not reconciled with the retained results, and initialization detail is lost. These tradeoffs limit the overall gain to a modest improvement.
